adultReview.scope: adult band only; youngerChild/olderChild remain unsigned and gated by PAEDIATRIC_TEWS_SIGNED_OFF
adultReview.decision: Adult chart to match the published SATS TEWS: every parameter scored 0-3, unsigned, 0 = normal (Rominski et al., Afr J Emerg Med 2014, doi:10.1016/j.afjem.2013.11.001). Replaces a -3..+3 transcription in which the symmetric 3 2 1 0 1 2 3 column header was read as signed and several rows were shifted one column.
adultReview.howRecorded: Verbal direction during review, relayed in the engineering session; no per-cell entries were made on the review page, which stated that unmarked rows accept the SATS column as shown.
adultReview.pending: Written signature on the regenerated docs/clinical-review/TRIAGE_SAFETY_REVIEW_PACKET.md section 1, including confirmation of each cell against the SATS manual (PubMed confirms the 0-3 structure and some cells, not every cell).

sourceCitation: Emergency Medicine Society of South Africa. The South African Triage Scale — Training Manual 2012. Twomey M, et al. Vital signs for children at triage: a multicentre validation of the revised South African Triage Scale (SATS) for children. S Afr Med J 2013.
notes: AH-47 gap report. Transcribed from a clinician-facing specification artifact (see docs/ENGINEERING_PLAN.md §11 follow-up), not yet reviewed against the primary SATS manual by a named, registered clinician. Do not treat as clinically authorized until reviewedBy/reviewedOn/version are filled in by that review. Numeric ranges use gte/lte/gt/lt (inclusive/exclusive) matching the source table's own symbols. Categorical parameters (avpu, mobility, trauma) score 0 when the value is unknown/not supplied — treated as 'not scored', not assumed normal. IMPORTANT INTERPRETATION FLAG for the reviewing clinician: the total score sums the ABSOLUTE VALUE of each numeric physiological parameter's matched score (heartRate/respiratoryRate/temperature/systolicBp), not the signed value — a literal signed sum would let severe bradycardia and severe tachycardia cancel each other out, which cannot be the real algorithm. AVPU/mobility/trauma keep their signed score as-is (ordinal, one best state and one worst, not bidirectional). Please confirm both of these against the primary manual — see tews.ts's contributionOf() for the exact logic.
